hot_size_model.interpretation: Steady-state HOT population is expected to be roughly 13,859,258 rows (~1.94 GiB) under average ingest, rising to ~31,395,736 rows under sustained high-activity days -- a small, BOUNDED fraction of the eventual total table size, versus the CURRENT architecture where 100% of 5,221,462+ rows (and growing) live in HOT forever.

cold_growth_model.note: COLD growth continues indefinitely in absolute terms (more segments accumulate) -- this is EXPECTED, not a failure; each segment is small, closed, and independently retireable, so it does not carry the same lock/backup/VACUUM burden as the monolithic HOT file. Moving data COLD does not eliminate total storage growth (explicitly acknowledged per Part 24's instruction) -- it converts unbounded HOT growth into bounded HOT + independently-manageable COLD growth.
future_cold_policy_requirements_not_acti: retention duration for COLD segments (e.g. retain N years before considering compaction)
compaction of many small/sparse segments into fewer larger ones if segment count becomes unwieldy
whole-segment retirement criteria (age + zero-reference proof, reusing the P2 Part 1 mechanism)
permanent-pinned-evidence extraction if a COLD segment is ever retired but some of its rows are later found to match a NEW pinning dimension not known at archival time

permanent_growth_quantified.assessment: This is genuine, valuable intelligence growth (confirmed operations, discovery evidence, direct/2-hop funding lineage) -- NOT reducible to zero without discarding real evidence. Whether it is further reducible via COMPACT_EVIDENCE_INDEX (storing only signature+minimal identity for replay rather than the full row) versus keeping full normalized rows hot is flagged as a P5+ optimization question, not decided here.
